question: On Tuesday, 3 February 2026, an event was held in the EP on the ‘global rise of right-wing populism’, organised by the NGO ECPS (European Centre for Populism Studies) and hosted by MEPs Radan Kanev (EPP) and Valerie Hayer (Renew).

The ECPS Annual Activity Report 20251 states the following in terms of its objective, ‘confronting the global rise of populism’: ‘[We] actively participate in numerous EU-funded and EU-oriented project proposals under Horizon Europe, CERV, Creative Europe, Erasmus+ and related frameworks’, ‘[We] engaged in proposals across major EU funding frameworks’.
It appears that EUR 269 125 was paid out for the ‘Encode’ project and EUR 18 500 for the ‘Untold Europe’ project, among others. In view of this: 1.
Can the Commission indicate for which ECPS projects or projects in which ECPS participates funds have been or will be disbursed, and what amounts are involved?
Can the Commission indicate whether it considers ‘confronting the rise of populism’ to be so important that it expressly wishes to finance this effort through an NGO such as ECPS?

Among other things, Special Report 35/20182 of the European Court of Auditors showed that there is a lack of transparency regarding the implementation of EU funds through NGOs. Does the Commission share this view?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.4.2026) The ECPS (European Centre for Populism Studies) is the beneficiary of one running grant for the implementation of the project Uncovering Neglected Truths and Outlining Legacies of Decolonization (UNTOLD Europe1) awarded under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme (CERV)2. The funding earmarked for ECPS amounts to EUR 18 500.

ECPS is a beneficiary of the grant for the completed project Unveiling emotional dimensions of politics to foster European democracy (ENCODE3) awarded under the Horizon Europe programme4. Its share of funding amounts to EUR 269 125. The objectives of EU funding are defined in programmes such as the CERV Programme, which are adopted by the European Parliament and the Council.

The programmes are implemented through work programmes approved by representatives of the Member States and open calls for proposals. Proposals are evaluated, based on pre-announced selection and award criteria along the rules and principles set in the Financial Regulation5.

The award of a grant is the outcome of a highly competitive process at the end of which the highest ranked proposals that best align with the objectives of the programmes are selected for funding. The Commission is fully in line with all the transparency requirements as they were written by the co-legislators.

Information about the beneficiaries of funding is published on the Financial and Transparency System and project related information is published on the Funding and Tenders portal6. The Commission refers to its replies to the Special Report 35/2018 of the European Court of Auditors (ECA)7. The Commission accepted three out of
